newsitem.title: UK: Nomura drops in London after JGB ban news.
newsitem.headline: Nomura drops in London after JGB ban news.

text.p: Shares in Nomura Securities Co Ltd were under pressure in London after news that Japan's biggest stockbrokers had been barred from participating in Japanese Government Bond (JGB) auctions.
The shares were trading at 1,525 yen by 1145 GMT compared with a Tokyo close of 1,550.
"It's not good news but not completely unexpected," one dealer said. "What the market is waiting for now is the complete list of sanctions."

Japan's Ministry of Finance said on Tuesday that it was suspending Nomura from JGB auctions and bond underwriting until the implementation of administrative punishments against the brokerage proposed by the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission(SESC).
The Japan's securities watchdog filed complaints with prosecutors on Tuesday alleging that Nomura and three former executives made illegal payments to a client.
While the SESC did not identify the client, he is believed to be one of Japan's 'sokaiya' racketeers, who extort money from corporations by threatening to disrupt shareholder meetings.
Nomura's shares were hit in March when the company admitted that two of its directors were involved in transferring Nomura money into the account of a corporate client linked to a sokaiya racketeer.

The shares, which had traded around 1,690 yen before the admission, crashed to a 1997 low of 1,120 yen on April 15 but had clawed back much of that loss in line with strengthening world stock markets.
"Today's drop has to be seen in that context," another dealer said. "The shares have done very well the past month so a bit of a drop on news like this is not that bad."
